'''Geoff LaTulippe''' is an American [[screenwriter]] and [[film director]] best known as the writer of the 2010 film ''[[Going the Distance (2010 film)|Going the Distance]]''.

==Early life==
LaTulippe was born in [[Cleveland, Ohio]]. His father's job as a casket salesman caused his family to move across the United States between numerous cities before they settled in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=ddp>{{cite web|url=http://www.donedealpro.com/members/details.aspx?object_id=393&content_type=1|date=September 15, 2008|title=Geoff LaTulippe|first=Will|last=Plyler|work=Done Deal Professional|accessdate=April 23, 2014}}</ref> LaTulippe attended [[James Madison University]] in Virginia, where he studied film and writing.<ref name=ddp/>

==Career==
Shortly after moving to [[Los Angeles, California]], LaTulippe was hired as a [[script reader]] at [[New Line Cinema]], a job he was offered by his friend who worked at the studio. After working there for two years, he tired of the job, saying that it "start[ed] to suck away [my] creativity".<ref name=ddp/> In July 2008, he sold a [[spec script]] titled ''[[Going the Distance (2010 film)|Going the Distance]]'' to New Line Cinema, a story based on his friend David Neustadter's previous long-term relationship.<ref name=ddp/> The film was ultimately directed by [[Nanette Burstein]] and released in September 2010. After selling his first screenplay, he quit his job as a script reader and became a full-time writer.<ref name=ddp/>

It was announced in 2009 that LaTulippe would write a [[film adaptation]] of ''[[Breathers: A Zombie's Lament]]'', a novel by [[S. G. Browne]], although the film is yet to go into production.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://filmschoolrejects.com/news/diablo-codys-breathers-announcement.php|date=February 24, 2009|title=Diablo Cody Tattoos Her Name on Zombie Romcom ‘Breathers’|first=Neil|last=Miller|work=[[Film School Rejects]]|accessdate=April 23, 2014}}</ref> In 2011, he was approached by the talent agency [[William Morris Endeavor]] (WME) to create a humorous short film about their company.<ref name=thr>{{cite web|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/going-distance-geoff-latulippe-directing-wme-paramount-287697|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=Todd|last=Gilchrist|date=February 7, 2012|title='Going the Distance' Screenwriter Geoff LaTulippe Lands Directing Gig at Paramount|accessdate=April 23, 2014}}</ref> The result was ''Yom Kippur at WME'', which starred [[J. B. Smoove]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slashfilm.com/watch-short-film-going-distance-screenwriter-geoff-latulippe-directing-gig-paramount/|date=February 8, 2012|work=[[/Film]]|title=Watch the Short Film That Got ‘Going the Distance’ Screenwriter Geoff LaTulippe A Directing Gig at Paramount|first=Germain|last=Lussier|accessdate=April 23, 2014}}</ref> The short film's popularity snowballed and it caught the attention of Adam Goodman, the president of [[Paramount Pictures|Paramount Film Group]], who then contacted LaTulippe to offer him a job as a [[film director]].<ref name=thr/> In 2012 Paramount announced that LaTulippe would direct an as-yet unnamed film for the studio.<ref name=thr/>
